prompt:
Pixel art emblem of the zodiac sign CANCER: a crab seen from above, its round shell in the centre, the two claws curving up and inward to form a protective circle, centred inside a thin-lined regular hexagon frame (all six sides equal) with a full moon directly above and a line of tide below behind it.

This is a SYMBOL, not a character: a timeless emblem like a heraldic crest, a carved totem, a stained-glass roundel or a constellation card. Front-facing, perfectly symmetrical, still and dignified. The face is calm and neutral with a steady level gaze, so that anyone born under the sign can see themselves in it. No cartoon expression, no grin, no frown, no eyebrows, no mascot, no cuteness, no story, no pose. Never fierce or scary: no fangs, no snarl. The sign's nature shows only through form: rounded, enclosing, shell-like curves: shelter, protection, the pull of the moon.

Style: bold simplified geometric shapes, 16-bit console pixel art, hard square pixels, no anti-aliasing, no blur, no gradients, no dithering. Drawn on a 96 x 96 pixel grid, shown enlarged so each pixel is a clear square. The whole image has a flat solid BLACK background, edge to edge.

Palette: exactly four flat colours plus black: pale silver, coral red, teal, deep blue. At most two flat shades of each, nothing else.

Composition: the emblem fills about 65% of the frame. Square image, no text, no letters, no watermark, no signature.
